questions.stem: Which of the following is a direct tax in Nigeria?

options.text: Value Added Tax (VAT)
Personal income tax (PAYE)
Excise duty on tobacco
Customs duty on imported cars

questions.explanation: Personal income tax is levied on a person's earnings and is paid by that person, typically through PAYE. VAT, excise and customs are levied on goods and services and can be shifted through the price, so they are indirect.

distractorRationale.a: VAT is an indirect tax on consumption
distractorRationale.c: Excise is an indirect tax on selected locally produced goods
distractorRationale.d: Customs (import) duty is an indirect tax on foreign goods

options.text: the average rate rises as income rises
everyone pays the same naira amount
the poor pay a larger share of income than the rich
the rate is a constant percentage of income

questions.explanation: Progressive tax systems take an increasing share of income as income grows, which is the structure of Nigerian personal income tax bands. A constant percentage is proportional; a heavier burden on the poor is regressive.

distractorRationale.b: A poll tax of equal naira is highly regressive relative to income
distractorRationale.d: A constant percentage is a proportional tax

questions.stem: A good sells for ₦5,000. After a tax of ₦500 per unit, the market price rises to ₦5,400. How many naira of the tax are borne by the consumer?
questions.explanation: The consumer's incidence is the increase in the price paid: ₦5,400 − ₦5,000 = ₦400. The producer bears the remaining ₦100, because ₦500 − ₦400 = ₦100. Incidence always adds up to the full tax.

questions.stem: Which of the following is one of Adam Smith's canons of taxation?

options.text: Equity
Devaluation
Credit creation
Comparative advantage

questions.explanation: Smith's four canons are equity (ability to pay), certainty, convenience and economy of collection. Devaluation, credit creation and comparative advantage belong to other topics entirely.

distractorRationale.b: Devaluation is an exchange-rate policy for the balance of payments
distractorRationale.c: Credit creation is a function of commercial banks
distractorRationale.d: Comparative advantage is a reason for international trade

questions.stem: If demand for a product is highly inelastic, an indirect tax on it will be borne mainly by

options.text: the consumer, through a higher price
the producer, who cannot raise the price
foreign governments
the Central Bank of Nigeria

questions.explanation: Inelastic demand means quantity falls only a little when price rises, so the seller can pass most of the tax forward. That is why petrol, tobacco and salt-type staples are attractive tax bases. Elastic demand would force the producer to absorb more of the tax.

distractorRationale.b: Producers bear the larger share when demand is elastic, not when it is inelastic
distractorRationale.c: Foreign governments are not parties to a domestic tax on a Nigerian good
distractorRationale.d: The CBN does not pay commodity taxes; it is the monetary authority

questions.stem: A uniform VAT on food that takes 8 per cent of a poor household's income but only 2 per cent of a rich household's income is

options.text: progressive, because the rich pay more naira
proportional, because the VAT rate on the till is the same
regressive, because the poor pay a larger share of income
a direct tax on personal income

questions.explanation: Progressivity is judged by the share of income taken, not by the naira amount or by the statutory rate on the receipt. Food is a larger fraction of poor budgets, so a uniform VAT on food is regressive even if the till rate is 7.5 per cent for everyone. It remains an indirect tax.

distractorRationale.a: A larger naira payment by the rich does not make a tax progressive if their income share is smaller
distractorRationale.b: A constant statutory rate can still be regressive in burden if spending patterns differ
distractorRationale.d: VAT is levied on goods, not on personal income, so it is indirect
